title: Evaluate Set Expression
description:
Given a valid set-algebra expression string `expr` composed of finite integer set literals (e.g., `{1, 2, -3}` or `{}`), binary set operators, parentheses `'('` and `')'`, and optional spaces, evaluate `expr` and return the resulting set as a **strictly ascending `int[]`**.

Operators and precedence:
- `'&'` (intersection): precedence `2` (highest), left-associative.
- `'|'` (union), `'-'` (set difference `A \ B`), `'^'` (symmetric difference): precedence `1`, left-associative.
constraints: Set literals contain comma-separated signed 32-bit integers (with optional spaces) inside '{' and '}'.
expr is a valid set expression.
hints: Parse each `{...}` literal into a hash set of integers and push it onto the operand stack; be careful not to confuse a negative sign inside `{...}` with the set-difference operator '-'.
Use Shunting-Yard with `'&'` having precedence 2 and `'|'`, `'-'`, `'^'` having precedence 1 (all left-associative), then sort the final set.

examples.explanation: Symmetric difference of {1,2} and {2,3} contains elements in exactly one set: [1, 3].
